request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Intersect Technical Steering Committee Support activities for 12 months across community engagement, protocol governance, and independent technical review.

claims.claim: Intersect requests $298,250, equal to 1,193,000 ADA, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.
The budget is allocated as 256,000 ADA for WP1, 832,000 ADA for WP2, and 105,000 ADA for WP3.
WP2 funds three specialist groups: the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, and Hard Fork Working Group.
WP3 funds a pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027 with formal conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.
Three TSC-related activities, technical workshops, the Security Council, and the Bug Bounty Programme, are funded separately through the main Intersect budget and are excluded from this request.

The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain submission under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The requested withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, potentially including deliverable verification, control testing, spend validation, and milestone evidence assessment.

The Technical Steering Committee has not received Cardano Treasury funding within the past 24 months, while Intersect and its committees received 22,385,000 ADA through listed prior governance actions.
Intersect will use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified reserve and project-specific addresses, multi-party authorization rules, and a public dashboard for auditability.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of Intersect Technical Steering Committee support, split across community-facing coordination, protocol governance and evolution, and a 2027 pilot technical review programme, with stated smart-contract administration, oversight, audit, NCL, prior-funding, and voting-process disclosures.
